input.quote: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
input.rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanism: the term is evergreen ("shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and Section 6(a) lets either party exit on fifteen (15) days' notice when no Statement of Work is outstanding, which is better than our 30-day opt-out and involves no multi-year renewal or non-renewal notice window. The pricing limb of the rule fails, however: because the term rolls on indefinitely, Contractor's unilateral right in Section 3(b) to "change rates with 30 days notice" is an uncapped, unlimited-frequency escalator, contrary to our position that continuing/renewal pricing be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Redline fixes rates within each SOW and caps increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, once per 12 months on 60 days' notice, with a 5% fallback.

ops.oldText: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
ops.newText: Rates set forth in a Statement of Work are fixed for the duration of that Statement of Work. Contractor may change rates for future Statements of Work no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least sixty (60) days prior written notice to Company, and any such increase shall not exceed the lesser of (i) the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The term is evergreen, so we have capped Contractor's unilateral rate changes at the lesser of CPI and 3% once per year with 60 days' notice, and fixed rates for the duration of each Statement of Work, consistent with our position that continuing engagements must be predictably priced. We can accept a 5% annual cap if that is easier for you.
proposal.summary: Cap Contractor's unilateral rate increases at lesser of CPI and 3% per year and fix rates within each SOW.
